Mga hakbang para maibsan at matugunan ang problema sa pagbaha ang tinalakay ng Metropolitan Manila Development Authority, sa pangunguna ni Chairman Atty. Don Artes, sa pulong ngayong araw kasama sina UP NOAH Executive Director Dr. Mahar Lagmay, Department of Environment and Natural Resources Usec. Carlos David, at iba pang ahensiya ng pamahalaan.

Sa pulong, ipinrisinta ni Chairman Artes ang mga ginagawa ng MMDA gaya ng mga proposed rainwater catchment facilities, isinusulong na drainage master plan ng Metro Manila, rehabilitasyon at upgrade ng Effective Flood Control Operation System (EFCOS), at ang panukalang Metro Manila Sponge City na layuning i-improve ang water retention at drainage ng NCR.

Ikinonsulta ni Atty. Artes ang nasabing mga proyekto, partikular ang rainwater catchment facilities kay Dr. Lagmay at hiningi ang expert opinion nito para matiyak na  nasa tamang design at gagana ang mga pasilidad.

Ipinakita naman ni Usec. David ang Road Inundation Map ng NCR habang si Dr. Lagmay naman ay ang mga road profile ng mga natukoy nang flood-prone areas.

Kanila ring binisita ang MMDA Communications and Command Center kung saan ipinakita ni Chairman Artes ang mga CCTV camera ng ahensiya na nagmomonitor sa trapiko at baha sa mga pangunahing lansangan sa NCR.

Pinag-usapan din ang iba pang areas for collaboration ng MMDA at ng UP Resilience Institute para sa mas epektibong flood management ng Metro Manila.

#mmda

data.text:
NATIONAL MINIMUM WAGE, WHY NOT?

Cong. Eli San Fernando is not getting much coverage except for very few social media platforms (pero grabe ang likes and positive engagement) and fewer traditional media outlets.

But he makes a great point here.

I’ve always wondered why the minimum wage was different in Metro Manila compared to other provinces or regions.

It’s a well known fact that because of the higher minimum wage, more people go here in NCR for work opportunities rather than in their home province (and then some go abroad).

This leads to trafficking, exploitation, informal settlers (because they have to find cheap rent in the city), congestion, and other issues.

The traditional neoliberal or liberal response has been - the cost of living and other economic variables are different in Metro Manila versus other provinces, that’s why the wages are lower outside of NCR because goods and expenses are cheaper there.

But is that really true anymore?

Maybe as to land value and rent. But the price of food, goods, and services in the provinces are definitely catching up to Metro Manila prices - and regardless, inflation outmatches the increase of wages over time.

And I know many well meaning friends and progressive people, especially from the kakampink side, who will be opposed to minimum wage.

I am not an economist and all the economic arguments will not make sense to me given this one simple fact that Cong. Eli San Fernando raises, which is - the blood, sweat, and tears of toiling 8 hours a day in Metro Manila is the same blood, sweat, and tears in the provinces.

Minimum wage mostly if not perfectly covers blue collar workers - physical hard labor work.

You have construction workers, fastfood workers, mall employees, and other laborers who have to physically work for 8 hours if not more because of exploitation (very few properly pay overtime - and even overtime rates would now differ between NCR and the provinces).

Physical work is physical work, where ever you are.

No one chooses to be born and raised in the provinces. They either have to suck up with a lower minimum wage as a construction worker in the provinces OR risk trafficking and exploitation and other issues to go to Metro Manila to work as the same construction worker but in the city.

I am not an economist so I would love to hear layman or simple explanations why a national minimum wage would work against the interests of the masses or blue collar workers.

I don’t care about businesses. In fact, if most of our economy is controlled by politico-oligarchs then they are profiting from an arbitrage because of the difference in minimum wages.

#EliSanFernando
#NationalMinimumWage
